summary.name: Sloth
summary.one_liner: Sloth is a free, open source native Mac app that lists all open files, sockets, pipes and devices used by running processes, built on the lsof command-line tool.
use_cases: Find which app is using a file or folder
Inspect network sockets held by processes
Debug files locked by running applications
Explore sockets and pipes between processes
Check open files as root for system troubleshooting
summary.what_it_does: Sloth displays all open files, directories, IP sockets, devices, Unix domain sockets and pipes used by running processes on a Mac. Its outline view can be filtered by name, access mode, volume, type, location or regular expressions, and sorted by name, process ID, user ID, process type or bundle identifier. It shows IP socket status, protocol and version, and draws sockets and pipes established between processes. An inspection window gives detailed file, socket and process information, and a contextual menu offers file operations. The page describes it as a GUI built on top of the lsof command-line tool.
notable: Native Objective-C/Cocoa app, universal Intel/ARM build
Can run with root privileges via in-app authentication
caveats: Latest version 3.6 requires macOS 11 or later; older macOS 10.13-10.15 need version 3.4, and 10.9-10.12 need version 3.2
Homebrew version may not be the latest release
